occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. Reasoning a trade out of the company they keep would be inventing one, so the vocabulary's own word for an absent record is what stands here.

READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Boyer, John K.” (poll_1834_018, line 187). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 12 times, as “BOYER JOHN K”, 1833-10-22 to 1836-06-29: 2 federal land entries — E2NE sec 14 T38N R14E; SE sec 20 T40N R14E and 1 lot in the platted town — lot 2 of block 12 in the town the register codes CHIV (L2BL12CHIV, as printed) and 9 parcels of the school section — lot 4 of block 94 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 4 of block 95 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 5 of block 81 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 5 of block 95 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 6 of block 81 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 7 of block 48 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 7 of block 49 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 8 of block 48 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 8 of block 49 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 160.00 acres stated in all, for $2177.00 (ls0090, ls0091, ls0092, ls0093, ls0094, ls0095, ls0096, ls0097, ls0098, ls0534, ls0610, ls1007). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $1230.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: BOYER JOHN K matches J. K. Boyer: the forename names J. K. Boyer of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0373) BY A RESIDENCY TEST, NOT BY A TRADE. T-0376's pass mints the register's `new_resident` people whose trade the papers print; this one takes the rest, where there is no trade to anchor anybody and a printed name on its own proves only that a Chicago paper set the type. The test asks the corpus two questions instead: does it place this person inside the town and NOWHERE outside it, and does a second independent witness corroborate a bare 'Chicago' — an address at street level, print in two or more issues, or print beside two or more people this reconstruction already holds. THE CORPUS PRINTS THIS PERSON IN 2 SEPARATE ISSUES. A transient is printed once and is gone; recurrence across the run is the paper's own evidence that the town kept dealing with them. The household around them is a CONTAINER and not an argument: one member, no dwelling, no division, no family, no recorded trade, and every one of those absences written as unattested rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. That the person is a HOUSEHOLD is the one invention here and it is recorded as docs/LIBERTIES.md L213. tools/mint_placed_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
